cmimc-2018-power-01a.prompt:
**Permutations.** A permutation of a set $A$ is a bijection $\sigma:A\to A$. Permutations are multiplied like functions: $\sigma_1\sigma_2$ sends $a$ to $\sigma_1(\sigma_2(a))$ (first apply $\sigma_2$, then $\sigma_1$). $S_n$ is the set of permutations of $\{1,\dots,n\}$. A $k$-cycle $(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_k)$ is the permutation sending $a_1\mapsto a_2\mapsto\cdots\mapsto a_k\mapsto a_1$ and fixing every other element; two cycles are disjoint if they share no element.

Give an expression for $|S_n|$, the number of elements in $S_n$, in terms of $n$.

cmimc-2018-power-02.prompt:
**Permutations.** A permutation of a set $A$ is a bijection $\sigma:A\to A$. Permutations are multiplied like functions: $\sigma_1\sigma_2$ sends $a$ to $\sigma_1(\sigma_2(a))$ (first apply $\sigma_2$, then $\sigma_1$). $S_n$ is the set of permutations of $\{1,\dots,n\}$. A $k$-cycle $(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_k)$ is the permutation sending $a_1\mapsto a_2\mapsto\cdots\mapsto a_k\mapsto a_1$ and fixing every other element; two cycles are disjoint if they share no element.

Prove that every permutation of a finite set can be written as a product of disjoint cycles.
cmimc-2018-power-02.answer: Follow the orbit $x,\sigma(x),\sigma^2(x),\dots$ of each element; the orbits partition the set and $\sigma$ acts as a cycle on each orbit.

cmimc-2018-power-03.prompt:
**Concentration.** A deck has $2N$ cards labeled $1,1,2,2,\dots,N,N$ (cards with equal labels are indistinguishable). The deck is shuffled and laid face down. At each turn you pick two face-down cards and flip them face up. If they do not match, you flip them back over; if they match they stay face up for the rest of the game. The game ends when all cards are face up. You have a perfect memory.

Find a strategy that is guaranteed to finish the game in at most $2N$ moves.
cmimc-2018-power-03.answer: On turns $1,\dots,N$ flip positions $(2t-1,2t)$; this reveals the whole deck. Then flip the $\le N$ remaining matching pairs.

cmimc-2018-power-04.prompt:
**Concentration.** A deck has $2N$ cards labeled $1,1,2,2,\dots,N,N$ (cards with equal labels are indistinguishable). The deck is shuffled and laid face down. At each turn you pick two face-down cards and flip them face up. If they do not match, you flip them back over; if they match they stay face up for the rest of the game. The game ends when all cards are face up. You have a perfect memory.

Consider the following strategy: each turn you choose a pair of cards uniformly at random from the set of pairs of face-down cards, until all cards are turned face-up (each turn you play perfectly randomly, ignoring what you remember). What is the expected number of turns this strategy will take? (Give your answer in terms of $N$.)

cmimc-2018-power-05.prompt:
**Crazy concentration.** This is like concentration (with $2N$ cards labeled $1,1,\dots,N,N$ shuffled face down, flipping two face-down cards per turn, matches staying face up), except that a permutation $\sigma\in S_{2N}$, the *mystery permutation*, is fixed and hidden from the player. At the end of each turn the player closes their eyes and the cards are rearranged according to $\sigma$: the card in the $i$th position from the left is moved to the $\sigma(i)$th position. Face-up cards also move.

Show that if the mystery permutation $\sigma$ is told to you, then you can guarantee finishing the game in at most $2N$ moves.
cmimc-2018-power-05.answer: Use $\sigma$ to undo the shuffling: on turn $t$ flip positions $\sigma^{t-1}(p),\sigma^{t-1}(q)$ to look at the cards that were originally at $p,q$.

cmimc-2018-power-06.prompt:
**Crazy concentration.** This is like concentration (with $2N$ cards labeled $1,1,\dots,N,N$ shuffled face down, flipping two face-down cards per turn, matches staying face up), except that a permutation $\sigma\in S_{2N}$, the *mystery permutation*, is fixed and hidden from the player. At the end of each turn the player closes their eyes and the cards are rearranged according to $\sigma$: the card in the $i$th position from the left is moved to the $\sigma(i)$th position. Face-up cards also move.

Find a strategy which is guaranteed to finish crazy concentration (the mystery permutation is *not* known) in at most $(2N)\cdot(2N)!$ turns.
cmimc-2018-power-06.answer: Let $M=(2N)!$. Since $\sigma^M=\mathrm{id}$, play a normal concentration strategy only on turns $1,M+1,2M+1,\dots$ when the deck is back in its original arrangement.
